title: How dipolar interactions structure molecular droplets
abstract: We investigate how dipolar interactions between microwave-shielded polar molecules structure the self-bound droplets formed under variation of the interaction strength. We identify the transition from droplets to crystals as a finite-size first order transition. With droplet-ring states and transitional supersolid states we predict additional structure in the crystal and droplet phases, respectively. To describe this strongly correlated regime, and in particular the reconfiguration of quantum ground states, we design a variational Monte Carlo framework based on neural quantum states. It is especially suitable to describe ground states and almost degenerate states with very different configurations. Moreover, one can easily determine the superfluid fraction. Our results reveal the sequence of finite-size structures through which dipolar interactions reorganize molecular droplets into crystals.

bite.hook: We uncover the sequence of finite-size structures through which dipolar interactions reorganize molecular droplets into crystals.
tldr: Investigated how dipolar interactions between microwave-shielded polar molecules structure self-bound droplets under varying interaction strength.
Designed a variational Monte Carlo framework based on neural quantum states to describe this strongly correlated regime.
Identified the droplet-to-crystal transition as a finite-size first order transition, predicting droplet-ring and supersolid states.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding how ultra-cold quantum molecules form complex droplets and crystals helps physicists simulate strongly correlated states of matter that are otherwise nearly impossible to calculate.
bite.eli5: Imagine trying to predict how a cluster of tiny, magnetic water droplets rearranges itself into a rigid grid. Researchers built a smart computer program using neural networks to figure out the exact steps these quantum droplets take when they freeze into crystals.
